text.headline: Machine Learning: Where it Started
text.text: This timeline illustrates the key milestones in the development of machine learning, from its inception to the present day. It includes different events and notable individuals that brought significant contributions for machine learning's evolution.

text.headline: The First Neural Network Model
text.text: Two pioneers, Walter Pitts and Warren McCulloch, developed the first mathematical model of a neural network in order to generate different algorithms that can mimic human thought processes.

media.credit: A video about Donald Hebb's work

text.headline: The Organization of Behavior
text.text: Donald Hebb, a canadian psychologist, published this book which introduced the concept of neuron communication. This concept focuses on the correlation between brain activities and neural networks.

media.credit: A video about Alan Turing's Turing Test

text.headline: The 'Turing Test'
text.text: The turing test was proposed by a british mathematician, logician, and computer scientist, Alan Turing. This proposal involves an evaluator that engages in text-based conversations between human and machines to determine which is which. He also developed the concept of 'Turing Machine' which is a model for modern computing.

text.headline: The 'Checker's Program'
text.text: This program was created by Arthur Samuel in the 1950s. It was one of the first computer programs that was able to play a perfect game of checkers by implementing different techniques such as the minimax algorithm and alpha-beta pruning. It can also improve itself based from its previous game experiences.

text.headline: The 'Perceptron'
text.text: Developed by Frank Rosenblatt in 1958, the Perceptron is a type of artificial neural network that is capable for performing different basic pattern recognition and other machine learning tasks. It consists of different key components that work together in order to process information and state predictions. It also became the foundation for modern neural networks.

text.headline: DENDRAL
text.text: Dendritic Algorithm (DENDRAL) is the first expert system that was created by Edward Feigenbaum, Bruce G. Buchanan, Joshua Lederberg and Carl Djerassi. It is specifically a chemical-analysis expert system in which it can analyze different chemical compounds and idenfity molecular structures, bringing a significant contribution to organic chemists.

text.headline: The 'AI Winter'
text.text: The Lighthill report criticized the state of AI research in the UK, leading to a decrease in funding and interest in the field. This period is often referred to as the 'AI Winter' due to the reduced optimism and progress in AI research. The report highlighted the limitations of early AI systems and the challenges in achieving human-like intelligence.

text.headline: The Resurgence of Neural Networks (1990s)
text.text: In the 1990s, neural networks regained their attention due to the rise of different internet-based services and digital data. One of the significant breakthrough was the existence of 'Backpropagation' algorithm which allowed for more efficient training of multi-layer or deep neural networks. This algorithm was mathematically formulated by Seppo Linnainmaa in his work on Automatic differentiation. However, it was popularized by Geoffrey Hinton and his colleagues in the 1980s.

text.headline: Deep Learning Revolution: The AlexNet
text.text: In this timeline, different deep learning techniques that contribute to a better pattern recognition capabilities and more advanced problem-solving emerge. This includes AlexNet, a deep learning model introduced by Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton. It is a model that is known for its capability of classifying and recognizing image with high accuracy.

text.headline: Transformers: The Discovery
text.text: Transformers was introduced by several google researchers, a deep learning architecture that aimed to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of natural language processing tasks. This discovery enabled faster trainings which led to different modern AI systems such as GPT.
